title: Tensor closure of the rational localizing categories
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], with $X$ a scheme in that setting. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite subextension of the fixed $\Qlb$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, using the condensed rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], respectively. In particular the latter uses continuous sections with image in a single finite subextension. The notation $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ means the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of the ambient unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ containing $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and closed under its small coproducts, as in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence].

1. $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is closed under $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ in
   $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.
2. For $A,B\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$, the derived tensor product
   $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B$, formed in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, lies in
   $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: For canonical finite-extension and finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure coefficients, clause (4) of finiteCoefficientDescentTwoColimit identifies finite-constant-model bounded constructibility with the upstream boundedConstructible predicate. Apply isMonoidal_boundedConstructible, specializing the scheme structure to aX and using ringChar k = p. This gives bounded tensor closure for each canonical coefficient.

For each allowed coefficient presentation, constructibleCoefficientTransport gives a strong monoidal derived equivalence preserving and reflecting finite-constant-model bounded constructibility. Apply canonical closure to the images of K and M, transport along the monoidal tensor comparison, and reflect membership. Repleteness comes from constantModelConstructibleFiniteTor_wellDefined. This proves clause (1) without changing either constructibility predicate.

Put R = Loc(Dbc). The inverse image of a localizing property by an exact left adjoint is localizing: shifts and triangles give triangulatedness, isomorphisms give repleteness, and preservesColimitIso identifies each image of an existing coproduct with the corresponding coproduct. Derived tensor is exact in either variable. The tensor-Hom adjunction gives the left adjoint for left tensor, and braiding gives it for right tensor.

Fix B in Dbc. Clause (1) and the inclusion Dbc ≤ R show that the localizing inverse image under right tensoring with B contains Dbc. The defining intersection minimality of localizingClosure gives R ≤ this inverse image. Now fix A in R. The first argument shows that the inverse image under left tensoring with A contains Dbc. Apply the same minimality to obtain closure for all B in R, proving clause (2).

proof_origin.place: Proof (1), existing bounded tensor closure after the proved rational constructibility comparison and coefficient transport; proof (2), both localizing minimality arguments.
